judged_text: The updateEvent fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` can never match, because that branch is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. When a booking reference has no externalCalendarId, updateEvent now sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API instead of the previous destinationCalendar.externalId, so reschedule/editLocation updates of pre-refactor bookings fail or hit the wrong calendar.

When a booking reference has no externalCalendarId, updateEvent now sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API instead of the previous destinationCalendar.externalId, so reschedule/editLocation updates of pre-refactor bookings fail or hit the wrong calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the updated `updateEvent` fallback is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. That fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId` equals `undefined`/`null`, which will almost always return `undefined`. Previously it fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (now effectively the first destination calendar). This means updates/deletes without an `externalCalendarId` (e.g., older booking refs) will not reliably target the intended destination calendar and may instead use `undefined` (or a later default) rather than the prior behavior.
